column2: On the authority of Abū Dharr Jundub ibn Junādah and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān Muʿādh ibn Jabal (may Allah be pleased with them both), from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: “Fear Allah wherever you are; follow a bad deed with a good deed and it will wipe it out; and treat people with good character.”
Reported by al-Tirmidhī, who said: A ḥasan hadith; in some copies: ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.

Ittaqi Allāh (“fear Allah”): by carrying out His commands and avoiding what He has forbidden. Ḥaythumā kunta (“wherever you are”): in whatever place you are. Wa-atbiʿ (“follow”): attach a good deed to the bad deed. Tamḥuhā (“it will wipe it out”): wipe out its bad effect on the heart and its punishment from the records. Al-sayyiʾah (“the bad deed”): the sin. Wa-khāliqi al-nās (“and treat people”): deal with them
bi-khuluqin ḥasan (“with good character”): by treating them as you would like them to treat you.
The command to fear Allah, which is the counsel of Allah, the counsel of His Messenger to his nation, and the counsel of every prophet before our Prophet ﷺ.
Doing a good deed after a bad deed wipes out the bad deed.
Encouragement to good character, because it is one of the qualities of taqwā.
Persevering in taqwā and being characterised by it in every situation, time and place.

In this hadith the noble Prophet ﷺ advises us to fear Allah in secret and in public, wherever the servant is, on land or sea, on the earth or in the air, alone or with people; and when the servant commits a sin, let him follow it with what wipes it out, repentance and seeking forgiveness:

“Indeed, good deeds do away with bad deeds” [Hūd 11:114]; and that he should treat people as he would like them to treat him, with a cheerful face, refraining from harm and giving sincere advice, so that hearts are brought together, love is made complete and the Muslims are united.
Indeed, taqwā is true honour and nobility, / while your boasting of this world is humiliation and want.
Whoever takes a means to salvation, / then the fear of Allah is the best of means.
No one rebukes the intelligent man like his own self, / and a man is set right by a righteous companion.
One who honours people is beloved to them; / whoever honours people, they love him.
